title: [CertiK｜低风险｜OTA-05][audit-fix] 历史 Q 被重新准入为 U 绕过证券控制
description:
## 来源与修复范围

来源：[CertiK TSV 初审报告（原始 PDF）](https://gitlab.okg.com/web3-dex/tsv/uploads/4b71892b28b1a3f8a9851a862d66ee15/CertiK-PRE-OKX-TSV---Audit__preliminary-20261030T231203Z.pdf)，第 26,27 页，编号 **OTA-05**，原报告等级 **Low**。原报告状态为 Pending；以下状态是 2026-10-31 独立代码复核结论，不代表 CertiK 已确认关闭。

**修复目标分支：`audit/2026-10-27-6402443-fix`（audit-fix）。请本项单独提交修复/验证记录，建立对应 MR，不与其他审计项混成一个不可独立验收的变更。**

- 报告审计 commit：`85623cd73ab6248b4acec71f478f30088c4deec3`。
- audit-fix 复核 commit：`543dcd34e882eead3a9f2391540c704105fbc693`。
- main 对照 commit：`a8bfc93aa2cf40142e6511e5069d90f65b59f420`；本 Issue 的修复目标是 audit-fix。

## 双基线复核

- **audit-fix：仍存在；文档要求限制准入**
- **main：仍存在；文档要求限制准入**

成立，属于管理员违反资产身份约束时产生的跨池控制缺口。已有注释是风险接受说明，不是链上修复。

### 原因与实现

disableQuoteTokenPoolRegister 将 Q.registered 清零但保留旧池交易。W/U 准入只拒绝当前 registered 的 Q，未永久记录曾经作为 Q。若旧 Q 再成为新证券 B 的 U，旧证券 A 的 W_A/Q 池仍把它当 Q，不经过 B 的股票侧许可、暂停和额度逻辑。

### 影响与利用前提

需要 SYMBOL_ADMIN 执行不兼容准入；普通用户不能自行把 Q 注册为 U。关闭新池准入并不移除历史池或改变历史资产身份。两个基线的 PermissionedValidationLib 都明确把这项规则交给治理。

## audit-fix 处理要求与验收条件

- [ ] 增加不可逆的历史 quote 身份记录，阻止曾作为 Q 的地址后续被准入为 U 或 W；关闭新池准入不得抹除该历史身份。
- [ ] 仅向后追加安全存储或使用审核过的命名空间；已部署代理的升级方案需从完整 QuoteTokenRegistered 历史回填，包括当前已禁用的 Q。
- [ ] 覆盖历史 Q 禁用后尝试成为 U/W 被拒绝，旧池按原生命周期继续交易，合法新 U/Q 不受影响。
- [ ] 在本 Issue 记录最终处理、对应 MR/完整 commit、验证命令与结果，并提供供 CertiK 复核的证据；已修复项以复核和回归补全验收，不制造无意义的重复代码改动。

### 修复建议及注意事项

若资产准入较频繁或由多个团队操作，建议增加不可逆的 everQuote 身份标记，禁止历史 Q 进入 U/W。既有部署升级必须从完整历史补齐，不能只读取当前 registered=true。若流程上接受，建立历史身份登记和准入检查，并向审计方按“已知风险/外部约束”说明，不能声称已修复。

OTA-05    OKX TSV - AUDIT


OTA-05             Historical Quote Reuse As Underlying Bypasses New Security
                   Controls




 Category          Severity     Location                                                                                  Status


 Design                Low      core/TSVRegistryV1.sol: 461~462; libraries/PermissionedValidationLib.sol:                    Pending
 Issue                          145~146


  Description


 TSVRegistryV1     assigns quote tokens Q to the non-stock side of W/Q pools and binds each permissioned wrapper W and
its underlying U to a security.  disableQuoteTokenPoolRegister          stops a Q from being used in newly registered pools while
deliberately preserving existing pools, whereas      registerPermissionedCurrency         is expected to prevent an asset from
acquiring a conflicting stock identity.

The quote-disable operation removes the only on-chain marker consulted by permissioned asset admission. An account with

 SYMBOL_ADMIN_ROLE      can therefore clear a historical Q's current registration flag even while an existing     W_A/Q   pool remains
active:


  // TSVRegistryV1.disableQuoteTokenPoolRegister(address,bytes32) —
  src/v1/core/TSVRegistryV1.sol:461-470
      function disableQuoteTokenPoolRegister(address quote, bytes32 reasonCode)
          external
          onlyRole(SYMBOL_ADMIN_ROLE)
      {
          _requireReasonCode(reasonCode);
          QuoteTokenRecord storage config = quoteTokens[quote];
          if (!config.registered) revert InvalidStatus();
          config.registered = false;
          emit QuoteTokenDisabled(quote, reasonCode);
      }


The project documentation explicitly prohibits reusing a historically registered quote token as W or U. However, this invariant
is enforced through the administrative admission procedure rather than by the contracts. The conflicting identity can therefore
be created only if an account holding     SYMBOL_ADMIN_ROLE      violates the documented admission rule and registers a verified
wrapper whose underlying is the historical quote token.

If the administrator subsequently registers a new wrapper       W_B   whose underlying is that Q,    _validateAssetIdentities
checks only the current    registered    value. Because the disable operation set this value to false, the historical quote passes
the identity check and becomes the canonical underlying of security B:

[PDF page 27]
OTA-05    OKX TSV - AUDIT





  // PermissionedValidationLib._validateAssetIdentities(address,address) —
  src/v1/libraries/PermissionedValidationLib.sol:150-157
          if (
              u.code.length == 0 || w == u || _isSystem(w) || _isSystem(u) ||
  r.getQuoteToken(w).registered
                  || r.getQuoteToken(u).registered || r.getUnderlying(w).securityId !=
  0
                  || r.getCurrencyUnderlying(u) != address(0)
                  || _readAddressArgument(
                          r.permissionsAdapterFactory(),
  IPermissionsAdapterFactory.permissionsAdapterOf.selector, u
                      ) != address(0)
          ) revert InvalidPermissionedConfig();


Existing pools retain the securityId     captured when they were registered. Their operation gate continues to evaluate that
stored security even after one of the pool assets acquires a new underlying role:


  // TSVRegistryV1._isOperationAllowed(bytes32,SecurityOperationCheckType) —
  src/v1/core/TSVRegistryV1.sol:810-819
          PoolRecord storage pool = pools[poolId];
          if (!isKnownPool(poolId)) return false;
          PoolLifecycle lifecycle = pool.lifecycle;
          if (checkType == SecurityOperationCheckType.TRADE) {
              if (lifecycle != PoolLifecycle.LIST) return false;
          } else if (checkType == SecurityOperationCheckType.LP) {
              if (lifecycle == PoolLifecycle.DELIST) return false;
          }
          return _isSecurityOperationAllowed(pool.securityId, checkType);
      }


As a result, Q can continue trading directly as the quote leg of the historical W_A/Q   pool while simultaneously serving as the
underlying of security B through   W_B . The historical pool remains governed and accounted for under security A: its lifecycle
and pause checks use A, its volume is charged to A's quota, and its multiplier and issuer permission checks apply to       W_A  .
Participants eligible for pool A can therefore trade Q without security B's pause state, quota, legal-share multiplier, or issuer
permission policy being applied. This leaves the underlying asset of security B circulating through a pool outside B's
compliance and accounting domain.


  Recommendation

Persist append-only asset-role markers such as     everQuote   ,  everUnderlying    , and  everWrapper   , set them when an
address first acquires each role, and reject every registration that would create a conflicting historical role. Before upgrading
existing deployments, derive and migrate these markers from quote records, underlying bindings, factory adapters, and all
stored pool keys, including disabled assets. Detect any pre-existing role collision during migration and pause the affected
pools until governance assigns unambiguous asset identities and reconciles their security and quota accounting.
